correctness.rationale: The original seven-base formula and all three limiting statements hold. For a sandwich with image {1,2}, fix the four values at those two domain points and compare f(a(g(x))) and g(a(f(x))). At every other domain point the same four possible fiber choices give the K base in the record; there are no constraints coupling different such points. The independent reconstruction exhausts all 94 equality-code/color assignments and recovers the 18 admissible types and their falling-factorial weights. Direct enumeration in a 3-point (1,2) example gives 133/729 commuting pairs. The supplied executable was inspected, not run; the reported direct enumeration concerns canonical representatives and one alternate placement, not every sandwich map. The corrected RESULT and VERIFICATION files state that scope, clarify the integral critical window as a limit along sizes including subsequences, and give uniform supercritical bounds. In detail, dividing each row by n^(2n-3) normalizes its base by n² and its prefactor by n. At fixed m only the large-block-square row is of order n^(-1) in probability. At m=log n+t+o(1), the all-equal, n times large-block, and large-block-square rows have normalized limits 1, 2e^(-t), and e^(-2t). In the supercritical regime, (1-m/n)^(n-2) ≤ e^(1-m) uniformly for m≤n/2; the three relevant error ratios are O(ne^(-m)), O(ne^(-m)), and O(n²e^(-2m)), and the other normalized bases are at most 1/2. These estimates establish the corrected text for the full regimes. No change to the count or asymptotic claimed.
